summary.text: A nymph of the Imbrasus near Parthenia who bore Poseidon the Argonaut helmsman Ancaeus, and by the same god was mother of Eurypylus, king of Cos slain by Heracles.

story.text: Apollonius, when Tiphys died among the Mariandyni, says Hera kindled courage in Ancaeus, whom near the waters of Imbrasus Astypalaea bore to Poseidon — the Samian helmsman who left Parthenia, the seat of Imbrasian Hera.
Apollodorus, telling how Heracles took Cos by night, names the slain king Eurypylus a son of Poseidon by Astypalaea.
